records.label: Main points and scope
records.note: This summary condenses the existing book. Small scope and evidence-led iteration are our recommendations, informed by the Astra game case study and instruction guidance. Skill availability does not establish selection accuracy or measured game improvement.

records.label: The short route through the full chapters
records.note: Each step links to the chapter containing its detailed rules, procedures, and evidence limits. The sequence, game, and optional trailer are worked proposals. Documentation supports the cited capabilities and deployment pattern; this summary adds no experiment or benchmark result.

records.label: The worked example and iteration method
records.note: The broken-game opening is an illustrative scenario. Signal Garden, the four-step loop, and the exercises are our teaching design. The sources motivate inspectable results and focused guidance; they do not validate this particular game.

records.label: Model, agent, and working agreements
records.note: Astra guidance covers initiative, instructions, delegation, and verification. MCP architecture distinguishes the host and exposed tools; a prompt alone cannot supply missing tool access.

records.label: Comparison and route selection
records.note: The six-way comparison, integration advice, and recommended combination are editorial judgments for this small game. They are not a measured ranking of prompting styles or single versus multiple agents.

records.label: What the implementation accounts establish
records.note: Spec Kit documents a workflow. The Astra game article and Anthropic accounts describe implementations. The March follow-up simplifies the workflow for a newer model; none supplies a controlled comparison of all six approaches.

records.label: Current evidence and older material
records.note: Dates and tested models determine relevance. Newer non-Astra results justify experiments, not claims about Astra game quality. Live reference pages are distinguished from dated publications.

records.label: Verified keynote passage
records.note: The mirrored keynote passage discusses verification workload and inspectable outputs. The runnable-milestone application is our interpretation, with current game practice supplied by the Astra case study.

records.label: Unavailable second transcript
records.note: The prior transcript passage could not be reverified and is withdrawn from the evidence. Current context advice is supported independently by source 17. No timecodes or video-only claims are invented.

records.label: Learning Godot and recording evidence
records.note: The written tutorials establish the learning sequence; current export docs establish deployment constraints. The research worksheet and experiment procedure are original tools for checking transfer to your project.

records.label: Stack features and teaching choice
records.note: Official sources establish rendering, engine, hosting, and lockfile behavior. Choosing a browser codebase and simple collision for Signal Garden is an editorial scope decision, not a performance benchmark.

records.label: Godot export constraints
records.note: Checked WebGL 2 Compatibility rendering, Godot 4 C# restrictions, threading/isolation, PWA workaround, and the HTML entry-name exception. Test the installed version and actual host.

records.label: Feasibility exercise
records.note: A tiny export tests the documented deployment constraints in your environment. Thirty minutes is a suggested investigation budget, not a supported completion estimate.

records.label: Git, remote repository, and Pages setup
records.note: Git references support initialization, complete staging, and reviewing staged content. GitHub CLI documents remote creation. Pages is a separate static publication step. Example commands require actual scaffold files and authenticated tools.

records.label: Repository layout and handoff
records.note: Scoped instructions and skill discovery have documented locations; the rest of the directory layout is a proposal. Progress artifacts come from the long-running-agent account. Revert records an undo, but conflicts and dependent changes still need review.

records.label: The fixed-camera experiment and PR
records.note: Branch and PR options are documented. The paths and camera change are illustrative and must match actual files. The body file must be written before gh pr create reads it.

records.label: Availability, invocation, and repository instructions
records.note: Codex supports eligible implicit matching and explicit selection, with a budgeted catalog. Repository conventions and skills have different roles. Remotion replaces a documentation integration; Comfy exposes action tools. These do not prove universal redundancy.

records.label: Evidence for conditional skill value
records.note: Benchmarks differ in tasks, models, skill construction, and discovery. Their findings cannot be pooled into an Astra performance claim. OpenAI’s Astra instruction audit is first-party guidance, not an independent gain measurement.

records.label: Optional game review skill and local comparison
records.note: The skill’s round rules belong to the original game brief. The proposed comparison tests whether guidance adds value in your actual setup; it has not been run for this book.

records.label: Player promise, mechanics, and boundaries
records.note: All game values, rules, loss precedence, pause/restart transitions, and exclusions are authored design targets. No external source establishes that three cells, 90 seconds, or this arena will be enjoyable. Verify implementation against this brief, then evaluate it through playtesting.

records.label: Using visual references
records.note: The Astra case study uses player experience and visual references. Assigning each reference a specific job and comparing a consistent camera view are our practical recommendations, not measured effects.

records.label: Input packet and prompt designer
records.note: The downloadable meta-prompt is authored for Signal Garden. Current guidance motivates explicit intent and relevant context. No reviewed experiment proves a meta-prompt beats a direct request on Astra.

records.label: Reviewing and refining a generated prompt
records.note: The review questions, one-pass exercise, and versioning procedure are proposed safeguards against contradictions and excess process. Source accounts motivate revisiting scaffolding; they do not prescribe this exact checklist.

records.label: Compact and bootstrap execution prompts
records.note: Both templates are manually authored and unbenchmarked. The compact prompt relies on existing accurate project files; the bootstrap carries the original game rules because those files do not yet exist.

records.label: Working agreements and evidence-based repair
records.note: Astra documentation supports initiative and proportionate testing; the game case study supports observable state and real controls. The coordinate rules, milestone order, and repair template remain project choices.

records.label: Reproducible setup and stable motion
records.note: A committed lockfile and elapsed-time animation have documented behavior. M0–M1 define proposed checkpoints, including explicit pause/resume policy for background time.

records.label: Playable win slice, then complete loss rules
records.note: M2 is deliberately incomplete: it establishes the win loop, timer display, and restart. M3 adds drone/health pressure and both loss conditions. Compare the final implementation with chapter 7’s single authoritative rules.

records.label: Art, audio, motion, and release
records.note: Browser docs support autoplay handling and reduced-motion detection; Pages/Vite docs support the release path. Visual targets, human playtesting, and milestone acceptance are our design recommendations.

records.label: Rules, real controls, and visible state
records.note: The Astra example distinguishes deterministic setup from real-control journeys. The table and snapshot are original acceptance tools for the chapter 7 design, not evidence of a game already tested.

records.label: Performance observation
records.note: MDN establishes callback timing and background behavior. The 95th percentile, 33 ms target, and 60-second sample are proposed choices. Callback intervals must not be reported as GPU duration.

records.label: Human playtest worksheet
records.note: The worksheet asks for observed experience and evidence. Implementation accounts motivate evaluation, but a small playtest does not establish population success rates or an objective fun score.

records.label: Failure classification, prompt revisions, and rubric
records.note: The examples and 0–2 rubric are authored comparison aids. Human judgments should remain visible; no measured experiment produced the V0–V3 sequence.

records.label: Fair comparisons and retiring redundant guidance
records.note: Varying model/task findings justify controlling the starting revision, tools, and budget. Repetition and transparent intervention records improve the comparison; the book reports no new Astra benchmark.

records.label: Static hosting, repository base, and workflow
records.note: Checked Pages’ static role, Vite project base, lockfile install, and artifact/deploy requirements. The linked book workflow is the actual implementation; the game snippet is an example.

records.label: Publication and public verification
records.note: The release prompt and full-play sequence are original verification procedures. Successful CI alone does not demonstrate gameplay; the expected revision and its assets must be checked at the public URL.

records.label: Recovery
records.note: Git revert records an undo and the workflow publishes another artifact. Restoration still requires a successful deployment and a check of the repaired public result.

records.label: Process diagrams and bounded decisions
records.note: Mermaid documents text-to-SVG rendering. The graphs describe observable decisions, not private model reasoning or executable automation. Success, effort limits, and blocked progress all have explicit outcomes.

records.label: What flows between the layers
records.note: The documented roles distinguish conventions, optional procedures, tools, MCP, lifecycle hooks, and workflow nodes. Our graph is a simplified data model, not a claim that every host exposes every integration.

records.label: Choose help and improve the cause
records.note: The routing questions and decision record are our practical synthesis. Documentation-only MCP deprecation and action-capable MCP are different cases. Diagnose access, context, or implementation before adding procedures.

records.label: Route comparison and storyboard
records.note: The unidentified page cannot be named with certainty. Product capabilities are documented; the comparison, shot manifest, and 3/3/4-second storyboard are original proposals. No video has been generated for this book.

records.label: Remotion composition and Comfy generation
records.note: Checked scaffolding commands, skills, template requirements, cloud MCP setup, API-format JSON, and output download behavior. The Comfy drawing is conceptual; cloud template availability must be discovered. The Remotion video transcript was not retrieved.

records.label: Runway jobs and n8n orchestration
records.note: Checked endpoint roles, asynchronous states, polling/error guidance, output expiry, and HTTP/Wait node behavior. The bounded recovery flow is proposed, not an executed n8n export. Multi-shot generation is separate from composing real gameplay capture.

records.label: Hooks, execution prompt, and final review
records.note: PostToolUse happens after the tool and cannot reverse its action. The validator, prompt, and review exercise are original. Pages serves static results; no hook, paid job, or video pipeline was run for this book.
